b:
O God,
whom I have felt to be one,
if you exist,
you who dwell
even in the atom,
I thought of you
every day;
for a while
I reviled you;
O pearl
of the shell of memory
who stayed in my thoughts
even in my reviling:
a few troubles
from the sacrificial fire of my thinking
I have joined with the pure Tamil words
that the Sangams nurtured,
made into a fine garland,
and laid at your feet;
won't you speak
a holy word
for all to hear?

I, who thought to bring up
the treasure in the well of the mind
called medicine,
stumbled and fell;
I, who leapt high hurdles,
have become mute;
holding my breath
I dived for pearls,
and yet, amazingly,
many years later
I still cannot find the bottom;
on every road that surrounds me
I met many trials
and lost even myself;
when will this thirst
for an MBBS be quenched?

Today, they say,
even in the White House
there is the blood of brave Tamils;
oh, what a pity!
The Dravidianism
that paints caste
on the very crowd that rules
next door
goes searching for a Tamil woman
in America:
what a disgrace.
Back then,
Tamil was spoken with Navi Pillay,
and four years later
all that is left is a muddied pond;
has the confusion cleared?
Only Diwali got the light.
Even if they come to power there,
will the scene change here?
Lord, only you can see.

We made night
look like day;
we made Kathirkamam's Kanda
appear in California;
we built sky-high towers
that amaze even Indra;
we built aircraft
and conquered the sky;
we brought down
the kings who ruled the earth
and said the people's verdict
is God's verdict;
this is the age of a historic race
that has seen many achievements;
Sankara, when will you
come to join us?

This I wrote as your devotee,
for Zhagaram, summit of pure Tamil,
at a small bell of a poetry offering
note: Written around the 2020 US election, when Kamala Harris, whose mother was Tamil, became Vice President. Navi Pillay, a South African of Tamil descent, was UN High Commissioner for Human Rights and pressed Sri Lanka on war crimes. Kathirkamam's Kanda is Murugan of the Kataragama temple in Sri Lanka. "The people's verdict is God's verdict" is a famous Tamil political slogan. The letter ழ (zha), unique to Tamil, is often called its crowning sound; "Zhagaram" appears to be the name of the poetry event.
